'''Ulukwumi''', also known as '''Olùkùmi''', is a [[Yoruboid languages|Yoruboid]] language spoken by the [[Olukumi people]] of [[Aniocha North]] LGA, [[Delta State]], Nigeria.

''Olùkùmi'' means 'my friend' in the Owé dialect of Yoruba and Igala.

==Vocabulary==
Below are some Olùkùmi words compared with the other [[Yoruboid languages]] Yorùbá (standard dialect), Òwé (a Yoruba dialect spoken in Kabba district of [[Kabba-Bunu]] LGA, [[Kogi State]]), and Igala, as given by Arokoyo (2012):<ref name="Arokoyo">Arokoyo, Bolanle Elizabeth. 2012. ''A Comparative Phonology of the Olùkùmi, Igala, Owe and Yoruba Languages''.
